6203.stem:
Farmer Ellis wishes to use the region for livestock. Knowing that he can fit 12 sheep per hectare (10,000$\text{m}^2$), he figures that he can fit a flock of 660 sheep. He didn't have Six Maps to calculate the area, so he used the method and working out shown below:

\exfigure{3307_q3_1}

figures.cap: Triangle with sides a, b, c and Farmer Ellis's handwritten working
Triangle with blanks for angles A, B, C and sides a, b, c

parts.latex: Explain why Farmer Ellis is most likely incorrect with his area calculation:
Using the cosine rule and your measured side lengths on the previous page, find the size of the angle opposite side c in the triangle, rounding your answer to the nearest minute.
Calculate the area of the field. Round to the nearest 100$\text{m}^2$.

Using the sine rule for at least one angle, calculate the other two angles in the triangle to the nearest minute. As such, complete the triangle below.

\exfigure{3307_q3_2}

solutions.latex:
Farmer Ellis has assumed the paddock has a right angle and has used side $c$ as the height, which is the wrong formula.

He should have used

$$A = \dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C$$

Using the cosine rule for the angle opposite side $c$:

$$\begin{aligned} \cos C &= \dfrac{a^2 + b^2 - c^2}{2ab} \\ &= \dfrac{1290^2 + 1260^2 - 880^2}{2 \times 1290 \times 1260} \\ &= 0.762\ldots \end{aligned}$$

$$\begin{aligned} C &= \cos^{-1}(0.762\ldots) \\ &= 40^\circ 21' \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct use of the cosine rule, or equivalent merit

solutions.latex:
Using the area formula with the included angle $C$:

$$\begin{aligned} A &= \dfrac{1}{2}ab\sin C \\ &= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1290 \times 1260 \times \sin(40^\circ 21') \\ &\approx 526\,200 \text{ m}^2 \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Correct substitution into the area formula, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source had no criteria; rubric written by us (2 marks per the question).

solutions.latex:
Using the sine rule:

$$\begin{aligned} \dfrac{\sin B}{1260} &= \dfrac{\sin 40^\circ 21'}{880} \\ B &= \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\sin 40^\circ 21'}{880} \times 1260\right) \\ &= 67^\circ 59' \end{aligned}$$

Using the angle sum of a triangle:

$$\begin{aligned} A &= 180^\circ - 67^\circ 59' - 40^\circ 21' \\ &= 71^\circ 40' \end{aligned}$$

The completed triangle has

$$\begin{aligned} A &= 71^\circ 40' & a &= 1290 \text{ m} \\ B &= 67^\circ 59' & b &= 1260 \text{ m} \\ C &= 40^\circ 21' & c &= 880 \text{ m} \end{aligned}$$
criteria: Finds one angle using the sine rule, or equivalent merit
Uses the sine rule, or equivalent merit

meta.format_note: Source's $B$ value appears slightly off if sine rule is used with side b over sin B (sin B = 1260 sin C / 880 gives about 111 or 69 degrees); kept as source.

3307_q3_1.notes: Drew the triangle with the vertices measured from the crop: thin 0.6pt lines (rule 3), labels a, b, c in maths italic at the crop's positions and clear of the sides (rules 11, 19). Farmer Ellis's working is in a plain rectangle at the same position: same lines, line breaks and alignment, fractions stacked (rule 23). The crop's wavy paper edge, the handwriting font and the scan's heavy triangle stroke are not copied (rules 3, 10, 19), and the working is typeset in the house font. The low overlay scores come only from the handwriting font versus typeset glyphs and the wavy border; the triangle and labels line up exactly.

3307_q3_2.notes: Triangle with six answer blanks ('Angle B:', 'Side c:' etc.) placed where the crop has them; text set flush right to each blank line. Letters are in maths italic (rule 19). Lines are 0.6pt (rules 1, 2, 3). The leftover overlay difference comes from the scan's thicker strokes and its sans-serif font.
